newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock drop expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock drop expected.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker after a day of lackluster trading with little sense of direction ahead of an anticipated draw in LME stocks Tuesday.
Traders expected the London exchange copper stocks to fall 2,000 to 4,000 tonnes.

Such a modest dip combined with reports that the Chinese felt copper prices were too high to prompt any buying at the moment, dampened market sentiment, Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
"This led to some additional profit-taking but it's a pretty bullish market overall. Demand remains quite firm," Raptopoulos said.
May COMEX copper settled 1.45 cents weaker at 109.95 cents, traded 111.90 to 109.05 cents. Spot March went out 0.65 cent lower at 114.65 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots compared to Friday's official 11,502 lots.
The backwardation on LME eased some $5 by COMEX close to $75/$80.
Trading was disrupted for about 40 minutes just after the opening due to technical problems at the exchange.
